questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Mass $M$ moves from $x = 0$ to $x = L$ with variable friction $\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x$ (where $\mu_k(L) = 0$). Total work done by friction is $n \mu_0 M g L$. The value of $n$ is:
questions.explanation: $W = \int_0^L (\mu_0 - \frac{\mu_0}{L}x)Mg\,dx = Mg\left[\mu_0 L - \frac{\mu_0 L^2}{2L}\right] = \frac{1}{2}\mu_0 MgL \implies n = 1/2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Mean free path in gas A is half of B ($\lambda_A = \lambda_B/2$), and molecular diameter $d_A = 2 d_B$. If number densities are $n_A, n_B$, the relation is:
questions.explanation: $\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi n d^2} \implies \frac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B} = \frac{n_B d_B^2}{n_A d_A^2} = \frac{n_B d_B^2}{n_A (4 d_B^2)} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{n_A}{n_B} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two identical inductors $L$ connected in series (config P) and parallel (config Q) with time varying current $I(t)$. Ratio of induced emfs $E_P / E_Q$ is:
questions.explanation: $E_P = (2L) \frac{dI}{dt}$. In config Q, each parallel inductor branch carries current $I/2$, so $E_Q = L \frac{d(I/2)}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} L \frac{dI}{dt} \implies E_P / E_Q = 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Number of nodes for 5th harmonic of open pipe is $n$, and for 9th harmonic of closed pipe is $m$. Ratio $n/m$ is:
questions.explanation: Open pipe: 5th harmonic has 5 nodes ($n=5$). Closed pipe: 9th harmonic has 5 nodes ($m=5$). Ratio $n/m = 5/5 = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Long solenoid of length $l$, radius $r$, turns per unit length $n$. Inductance of solenoid is:
questions.explanation: $L = \mu_0 n^2 A l = \mu_0 n^2 (\pi r^2) l = \mu_0 \pi n^2 r^2 l$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Light source power decreases linearly with time. Variation of photocurrent $I$ and stopping potential $|V|$ with time is:
questions.optionA: Photocurrent $I$ decreases linearly while stopping potential $|V|$ remains constant (Graph 1)
questions.explanation: Photocurrent is proportional to light intensity (power), whereas stopping potential depends solely on photon frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Capacitors P, Q (series) and S (parallel), each $C$, connected to battery $V$. Ratio of energy in P ($U_P$) to total energy ($U_T$) is:
questions.explanation: $V_P = V/2 \implies U_P = \frac{1}{2}C(V/2)^2 = \frac{1}{8}CV^2$. $C_{\text{total}} = C/2 + C = 3C/2 \implies U_T = \frac{3}{4}CV^2 \implies U_P / U_T = (1/8)/(3/4) = 1/6$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Horizontal pipe: area $A_P = 40\text{ cm}^2, A_Q = 20\text{ cm}^2$, pressure difference $\Delta P = 15\text{ N/m}^2$. Flow rate in $\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$ is ($\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3$):
questions.explanation: $\Delta P = \frac{1}{2}\rho v_Q^2\left(1 - \frac{A_Q^2}{A_P^2}\right) \implies 15 = 500 v_Q^2 (3/4) \implies v_Q = 0.2\text{ m/s} = 20\text{ cm/s}$. Flow rate $= A_Q v_Q = 20 \times 20 = 400\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Circular loop radius $r$ carrying $I_0$. Resistance $R_{ABC} = R_{ADC}/2$. Magnetic field at centre O is:
questions.explanation: $I_1 = \frac{2}{3}I_0$ (semicircle ABC) and $I_2 = \frac{1}{3}I_0$ (ADC). $B_{\text{net}} = \frac{\mu_0}{4r}(I_1 - I_2) = \frac{\mu_0}{4r}\left(\frac{1}{3}I_0\right) = \frac{\mu_0 I_0}{12r}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In terminal velocity experiment ($v_t = \frac{2r^2 g}{9\eta}(\sigma - \rho)$), plot of $v_t$ vs density ratio $(\sigma/\rho)$ is:
questions.optionA: Straight line with positive slope cutting horizontal axis at $\sigma/\rho = 1$ (Graph 1)
questions.explanation: $v_t = \frac{2r^2 g\rho}{9\eta}\left(\frac{\sigma}{\rho} - 1\right)$, which is a linear equation with $x$-intercept at $\sigma/\rho = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Planets $P_1, P_2$ have equal mass and radii $R_2 = R_1/2$. Ratio of escape speeds $v_2 / v_1$ is:
questions.explanation: $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} \implies \frac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\frac{R_1}{R_2}} = \sqrt{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Time period of revolution of a planet in circular orbit of radius $R$ is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Kepler's third law: $T^2 \propto R^3 \implies T \propto R^{3/2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Wire A (mass/length $\lambda$, current $I$) on floor. Wire B ($2I$) at height $h$. Minimum height $h$ so wire A does not lift is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic upward force per length $= \frac{\mu_0 I (2I)}{2\pi h} = \frac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi h} = \lambda g \implies h = \frac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi \lambda g}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Zener diode with $V_Z = 3\text{ V}$ reverse biased with input $V_i = 5\text{ V}$ and series resistor $R$. Voltage across resistor $V_B - V_A$ is:
questions.explanation: Zener maintains $3\text{ V}$ across itself; remaining voltage $5 - 3 = 2\text{ V}$ drops across resistor $R$.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ strikes photocells with threshold $\lambda_1 < \lambda, \lambda_2 > \lambda, \lambda_3 \gg \lambda$. Stopping potentials relation is:
questions.explanation: For cell 1, $\lambda > \lambda_1 \implies$ no emission ($V_1 = 0$). For cells 2 & 3, shorter threshold $\implies$ smaller work function $\implies V_2 < V_3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Photon and electron each have energy $E = 20\text{ eV}$. Ratio of linear momentum $p_e / p_{\text{ph}}$ is ($c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}, m = 9 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$):

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Which of the following physical measurements requires 'Index Correction'?
questions.optionC: Focal length of lenses using optical bench
questions.optionD: Speed of sound by resonance tube
questions.explanation: Optical bench experiments require index correction to account for needle length and positioning relative to lens optical centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Point charge moved through dielectric sphere ($ho, R$) from $r=2R$ to $r=3R$. Total work done is $\frac{\rho R^2}{n \varepsilon_0}$. Value of $n$ is:
questions.explanation: $Q = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho$. $W = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{2R} - \frac{1}{3R}\right) = \frac{\rho R^3}{3\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{6R}\right) = \frac{\rho R^2}{18\varepsilon_0} \implies n = 18$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Three media P ($mu=1$), Q ($mu=1.25$, thickness $5\text{ cm}$), R ($mu=1.5$). Object at center of Q. Apparent depths $|h_1 - h_2|$ in cm is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two particles on unit circle move with equal angular speed in opposite directions from $\theta = \pi/2$ to $-\pi/2$. Total linear momentum $P(\theta)$ graph is:
questions.explanation: Horizontal momentum components cancel while vertical components add: $P = 2m v\cos\theta$, which produces a positive symmetric arch peaking at $\theta = 0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Temperature of metallic sphere of radius $R$ increases by $\Delta T$. With linear coefficient $\alpha$, volume increase is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta V = V \gamma \Delta T = \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\right)(3\alpha)\Delta T = 4\pi R^3 \alpha \Delta T$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Cylindrical cork oscillates with period $T$ in liquid $\rho_1$ and $2T$ in liquid $\rho_2$. Ratio $\rho_2 / \rho_1$ is:
questions.explanation: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{A \rho g}} \implies T \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}} \implies \frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = \left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Vernier caliper ($1\text{ MSD} = 1\text{ mm}, 10\text{ VSD}$). Zero of VS is left of zero with 4th division coinciding (negative zero error). Measured length is $1\text{ cm}$. Actual length:
questions.explanation: $\text{Zero error} = -(10-4) \times 0.1\text{ mm} = -0.6\text{ mm} = -0.06\text{ cm}$. $\text{Actual} = 1.00 - (-0.06) = 1.06\text{ cm}$ (Official key marked conceptual bonus/option 4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Solid spheres A ($M, R$) and B ($m, r$) attached along horizontal axis. Difference of moments of inertia $I_A - I_B$ is:
questions.explanation: $I_A = I_{cm,A} + I_{cm,B} + m(R+r)^2$ and $I_B = I_{cm,A} + I_{cm,B} + M(R+r)^2 \implies I_A - I_B = (m - M)(R + r)^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For simple harmonic oscillator ($m, k$), plot of $v$ vs $x$ is a circle. Then:
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: $\frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{v^2}{\omega^2 A^2} = 1$. For a circular graph, semi-axes must be equal: $\omega = 1 \implies \sqrt{k/m} = 1 \implies k = m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Lenses $L_1 (+10\text{ cm})$ and $L_2 (-10\text{ cm})$ separated by $3\text{ cm}$ with object at $30\text{ cm}$ from $L_1$. Final image position is:
questions.optionA: $20\text{ cm}$ to left of concave lens
questions.optionB: $60\text{ cm}$ to the left of the concave lens
questions.explanation: For $L_1$: $\frac{1}{v_1} - \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{1}{10} \implies v_1 = +15\text{ cm}$. Virtual object for $L_2$ at $u_2 = +(15 - 3) = +12\text{ cm}$. $\frac{1}{v_2} - \frac{1}{12} = -\frac{1}{10} \implies v_2 = -60\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: AC voltage $V = 220\sin(2 \times 10^3 t)$ applied to LCR circuit ($L = 10\text{ mH}, C = 25\,\mu\text{F}, R = 100\,\Omega$). Current amplitude is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Thin disc rotates about fixed center O. Angular momentum about A ($OA$) and B ($OB = 2 OA$) satisfies $L_A / L_B$ equal to:
questions.optionC: 1 (Angular momentum about any point is identical for pure rotation about fixed axis through COM)
questions.explanation: Since COM is stationary at O, linear momentum $\vec{P} = 0$, making total angular momentum independent of the reference origin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Loop area varies as $A(t) = A_0(1 + \sin t)$ in constant $B$. Power dissipated $P(t)$ vs time is:
questions.optionB: $\cos^2 t$ positive periodic waveform with $P=0$ when $dA/dt = 0$ (Graph 2)
questions.explanation: Induced EMF $\varepsilon = B \frac{dA}{dt} = B A_0 \cos t \implies P = \frac{\varepsilon^2}{R} \propto \cos^2 t$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Point charge $Q$ in cavity of solid conductor. Points B and C are equidistant from center outside. Electric fields satisfy:
questions.explanation: Inside cavity $E_A \ne 0$. Due to spherical electrostatic shielding, outside surface charge distributes uniformly, so $E_B = E_C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Charge $-q$ released from rest at $3R$ from center of fixed sphere with charge $+Q$. Speed at surface $R$ is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{Qq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{R} - \frac{1}{3R}\right) = \frac{2Qq}{12\pi\varepsilon_0 R} \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{Qq}{3\pi\varepsilon_0 m R}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In Geiger-Marsden $\alpha$-scattering, plot of scattered particles $N(\theta)$ vs scattering angle $\theta$ is:
questions.explanation: Rutherford scattering formula predicts $N(\theta) \propto \csc^4(\theta/2)$, showing sharp exponential-like fall from $0^\circ$ to $180^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Resistors with $+\alpha$ and $-\alpha$ in series (circuit A) and parallel (circuit B). As temperature increases:
questions.explanation: Series: $R_A = R_0(1+\alpha\Delta T) + R_0(1-\alpha\Delta T) = 2R_0$ (constant). Parallel: $R_B = \frac{R_0^2(1-\alpha^2\Delta T^2)}{2R_0} < R_0/2 \implies I_B$ increases.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: EM wave in medium ($\varepsilon_r = 9$) has $E_x = E_0\sin(kz - 2\pi \times 10^6 t)$. The INCORRECT statement is:
questions.optionB: The wavelength inside the medium is $300\text{ m}$ (Actual $\lambda = v/f = 10^8 / 10^6 = 100\text{ m}$)
questions.explanation: $v = c/\sqrt{9} = 10^8\text{ m/s}, f = 10^6\text{ Hz} \implies \lambda = 10^8/10^6 = 100\text{ m}$ (not $300\text{ m}$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Monatomic gas in rectangular PV cycle: $(V_1=2, V_2=5\text{ m}^3; P_1=100, P_2=300\text{ N/m}^2)$. Total heat supplied is:
questions.explanation: $Q_{\text{supplied}} = Q_{da} + Q_{ab} = n C_v \Delta T + n C_p \Delta T = \frac{3}{2}(2)(200) + \frac{5}{2}(300)(3) = 600 + 2250 = 600\text{ J}$ net.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Electron in excited Hydrogen atom has velocity $v = \sqrt{25.6} \times 10^5\text{ m/s} = 5.06 \times 10^5\text{ m/s}$. Radius is $x \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$ where $x$ is:
questions.explanation: $r = \frac{k e^2}{m v^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{9 \times 10^{-31} \times 25.6 \times 10^{10}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m} \implies x = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Banked racetrack of radius $50\text{ m}$ with zero friction tyre wear at $10\text{ m/s}$ ($g=10\text{ m/s}^2$). Banking angle $\theta$ is:
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{R g} = \frac{100}{50 \times 10} = \frac{1}{5} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(1/5)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Three diodes $D_1, D_2, D_3$ with reverse/forward bias across $5\text{ V}$. Depletion widths order is:
questions.optionC: $W_3 > W_2 > W_1$ (Reverse biased $D_3$ widest, unbiased $D_2$ intermediate, forward biased $D_1$ thinnest)
questions.explanation: Reverse bias widens depletion layer; forward bias narrows it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match EM Spectrum with Applications:
P. Microwave, Q. UV rays, R. Gamma rays, S. Radio waves
I. Water purification, II. Warming food, III. AM/FM broadcasting, IV. Cancer radiotherapy
questions.explanation: Microwave = Food warming (II), UV = Water disinfection (I), Gamma = Cancer therapy (IV), Radio = AM/FM communication (III).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Mass A ($m, 10\text{ m/s}$) hits suspended stationary bob B ($m, L=10\text{ m}$) elastically. Height $h$ bob rises is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: Elastic collision between equal masses transfers complete velocity: $v_B = 10\text{ m/s} \implies h = \frac{v^2}{2g} = \frac{100}{20} = 5\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Polyatomic gas has 3 translational, 3 rotational, and $f$ vibrational modes. If $C_P / C_V = 8/7$, value of $f$ is:
questions.explanation: $C_V = 3R + fR = (3+f)R, C_P = (4+f)R \implies \frac{4+f}{3+f} = \frac{8}{7} \implies 28 + 7f = 24 + 8f \implies f = 4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Benzene $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{COCl/AlCl}_3} \text{Acetophenone} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOCl}} P + Q$. Correct statement is:
questions.optionA: P is sodium salt, Q is primary alcohol
questions.optionC: If P gives benzoic acid on acidification, Q ($\text{CHCl}_3$) gives poisonous phosgene gas on exposure to air and light
questions.explanation: Haloform reaction yields sodium benzoate ($P$) and chloroform ($Q$). Chloroform oxidizes in light/air to poisonous phosgene ($\text{COCl}_2$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: $[\text{Fe(ox)}_3]^{3-}$ is chiral.
Statement II: $\text{trans}-[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{ox})_2]^-$ is chiral.
questions.optionC: Statement I is CORRECT but Statement II is INCORRECT (Trans isomer has plane/center of symmetry)
questions.explanation: Tris-chelate $[\text{Fe(ox)}_3]^{3-}$ lacks planes of symmetry and is optically active; trans-diaqua isomer has inversion symmetry and is achiral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Benzyl carbocation ($\text{Ph-CH}_2^+$) is stabilized by delocalization of empty p-orbital with:
questions.explanation: Carbocation empty p-orbital overlaps with aromatic ring filled $\pi$-bonding orbitals and adjacent filled C-H $\sigma$-bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In potash alum $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\text{H}_2\text{O}$, the ratio of $\text{K}^+$ to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions is:
questions.explanation: Potash alum contains $2\text{ K}^+$ and $4\text{ SO}_4^{2-}$ ions $\implies$ ratio is $2 : 4 = 1 : 2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which statement about peptides and proteins is TRUE?
questions.optionC: In $\beta$-pleated sheet structures, adjacent polypeptide chains are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds
questions.explanation: Beta-sheets are stabilized by inter-strand hydrogen bonds between backbone $C=O$ and $N-H$ groups.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Rounding 17.0145 and 21.0235 to three digits after decimal gives:
questions.optionC: 17.014 and 21.024 (Preceding digit 4 is even $\to$ unchanged; 3 is odd $\to$ rounded up to 4)
questions.explanation: By rounding rules for 5: if preceding digit is even (4), it stays 4; if odd (3), it rounds up to 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Correct decreasing order of solubility in water at $298\text{ K}$ ($K_{sp}: \text{AgBr}=5\times 10^{-13}, \text{Zn(OH)}_2=1\times 10^{-15}, \text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2=1.3\times 10^{-18}$) is:
questions.explanation: Solubilities: $\text{Zn(OH)}_2: s = (K_{sp}/4)^{1/3} = 6.3 \times 10^{-6}\text{ M} > \text{AgBr}: s = \sqrt{K_{sp}} = 7.1 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M} > \text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2: s = 6.9 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct decreasing magnitude trend of electron gain enthalpy among halogens is:
questions.explanation: Chlorine has highest electron affinity because compact $2p$ shell of fluorine experiences significant inter-electronic repulsion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: For ideal solution, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$.
Reason R: No intermolecular interactions occur between P and Q.
questions.optionA: Both A and R correct, R explains A
questions.optionC: A is correct but R is NOT correct (Interactions $P-Q$ equal $P-P$ and $Q-Q$)
questions.explanation: In ideal solutions, intermolecular forces exist and are identical in magnitude between like and unlike molecules ($A-B = A-A = B-B$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which amino acid gives blood-red colouration when its sodium fusion extract is treated with sodium nitroprusside?
questions.explanation: Methionine and Cysteine contain sulfur, yielding $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$ on fusion which gives purple/violet/red test with nitroprusside.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Standard electrode potential for $\text{Fe}^{3+} + e^- \to \text{Fe}^{2+}$ given $E^\circ(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}) = -0.04\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}) = -0.44\text{ V}$ is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta G_3^\circ = \Delta G_1^\circ - \Delta G_2^\circ \implies -1(F)E^\circ = -3(F)(-0.04) - [-2(F)(-0.44)] = 0.12 - 0.88 = -0.76 \implies E^\circ = +0.76\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $10\text{ mL}$ of $0.25\text{ M}$ oxalic acid is titrated with $10\text{ mL}$ of acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$. Molarity of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is:
questions.explanation: $5(M_{\text{ox}} V_{\text{ox}}) = 2(M_{\text{KMnO}_4} V_{\text{KMnO}_4}) \implies 2 \times 0.25 \times 10 = 5 \times M \times 10 \implies M = \frac{0.50}{5} = 0.10\text{ M}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Decreasing spectrochemical series order of ligands by crystal field splitting is:
questions.explanation: Spectrochemical order: Strong $\text{CO} > \text{CN}^- > \text{en} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{ox}^{2-} > \text{OH}^- > \text{F}^- > \text{Cl}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{I}^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Two moles of ideal gas undergo free isothermal expansion from $10\text{ L}$ to $100\text{ L}$. Values of $\Delta S_{\text{sys}}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{surr}}$ are:
questions.explanation: Free expansion does no work against vacuum ($q_{\text{surr}} = 0 \implies \Delta S_{\text{surr}} = 0$). $\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = n R \ln(V_2/V_1) = 2 R \ln(10) = 4.606 R$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For zero-order reaction $2A \to B$ with rate constant $k = 1.0\text{ M/min}$ and $[A]_0 = 2\text{ M}$, time for $75\%$ reaction completion is:
questions.explanation: Rate $= -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[A]}{dt} = k \implies -\Delta[A] = 2kt$. Consumed $= 0.75(2\text{ M}) = 1.5\text{ M} = 2(1.0)t \implies t = 0.75\text{ min}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: Generally, 3d transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R: Greater number of unpaired $(n-1)d$ and $ns$ electrons participate in strong metallic bonding.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: High enthalpy of atomization and melting point in d-block metals stems from covalent overlap of unpaired 3d and 4s electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Strong electrolyte XY has slope $-90.0$ in Kohlrausch plot $\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$. At $c = 0.01\text{ M}$, $\Lambda_m = 145.0$. If $\lambda^\circ(X^+) = 74.0$, $\lambda^\circ(Y^-)$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Amount of $\text{CO}_2$ evolved upon complete combustion of $116\text{ g}$ of n-butane ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}, M=58\text{ g/mol}$) is:
questions.explanation: $116\text{ g butane} = 2\text{ moles}$. $2\text{ mol } \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10} \to 8\text{ mol } \text{CO}_2 \times 44\text{ g/mol} = 352\text{ g } \text{CO}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Arrhenius plot with $E_a = 6.64\text{ kJ/mol}$ and intercept $\ln A = 6$. Temperature where $k = e^2\text{ min}^{-1}$ ($\ln k = 2$) is ($R = 8.3\text{ J/K mol}$):
questions.explanation: $\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT} \implies 2 = 6 - \frac{6640}{8.3 T} \implies \frac{800}{T} = 4 \implies T = 200\text{ K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Heating NaCl with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement II: Heating NaI with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ results in reduction of Mn.
questions.optionD: Statement I is INCORRECT (Mn is reduced from $+4$ to $+2$) but Statement II is CORRECT
questions.explanation: $\text{MnO}_2$ acts as an oxidizing agent, oxidizing halides to halogens ($2\text{X}^- \to \text{X}_2$) while Manganese is reduced from $+4$ to $+2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which coordination complex has the HIGHEST spin-only magnetic moment?
questions.explanation: $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ has 2 unpaired electrons (highest among the given low spin options).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which Lanthanide $+3$ ion possesses exactly FOUR unpaired electrons ($4f^4$ or $4f^{10}$)?
questions.explanation: Holmium $\text{Ho}^{3+} (Z=67)$ has configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^{10}$ with $(14-10) = 4$ unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct chemical formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is:
questions.explanation: Cobalt(III) coordination sphere is $[\text{Co}^{+3}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})(\text{Cl}^-)]^{2+}$, balanced by two ionizable chloride anions $\text{Cl}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reversible thermodynamic Carnot-like cycle with isothermal steps 1 & 3 and adiabatic steps 2 & 4. Net isothermal work is:
questions.explanation: For $1\text{ mol}$, isothermal reversible expansion work is $-R T_1 \ln(V_2/V_1) = -2 T_1 \ln(V_2/V_1)$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: First ionization enthalpy of Oxygen is lower than Nitrogen and Fluorine.
Reason R: Loss of one electron from $2p^4$ in Oxygen yields a stable half-filled $2p^3$ subshell.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has stable half-filled $2p^3$ configuration; removal of paired electron in Oxygen ($2p^4$) relieves electron-electron repulsion, yielding stable half-filled shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding liquid solutions:
A. Ideal solutions obey Raoult's law across all concentrations
B. Chloroform and acetone show negative deviation
C. Aniline and phenol show positive deviation (They show negative deviation)
questions.explanation: Aniline and phenol form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, exhibiting negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reaction of Cyclohexyl magnesium bromide with Aniline ($\text{Ph-NH}_2$) yields:
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent abstracts acidic hydrogen from amine amino group: $\text{R-MgBr} + \text{Ph-NH}_2 \to \text{R-H (Cyclohexane)} + \text{Ph-NH-MgBr}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding maximum covalency is TRUE?
questions.optionA: Boron has a maximum covalency of four (Uses one $2s$ and three $2p$ orbitals; lacks d-orbitals)
questions.explanation: Second period elements (B, C, N, O) lack d-orbitals in their valence shell, restricting maximum covalency to 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Protein thermal denaturation $N \rightleftharpoons D$ at $60^\circ\text{C}$ ($333\text{ K}$) has $K=1 (\Delta G^circ = 0)$ and $\Delta H^circ = 666\text{ kJ/mol}$. $\Delta S^circ$ is:
questions.explanation: $\Delta S^circ = \frac{\Delta H^circ}{T} = \frac{666\text{ kJ/mol}}{333\text{ K}} = 2.0\text{ kJ K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Chemical Species with Geometries:
A. $\text{PCl}_5$, B. $\text{BrF}_5$, C. $\text{BF}_4^-$, D. $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$
I. Tetrahedral, II. Square Planar, III. Trigonal bipyramidal, IV. Square pyramidal
questions.explanation: $\text{PCl}_5 = \text{TBP (III)}$, $\text{BrF}_5 = \text{Square pyramidal (IV)}$, $\text{BF}_4^- = \text{Tetrahedral (I)}$, $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-} = \text{Square planar (II)}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: trans-But-2-ene $+\text{Br}_2/\text{CCl}_4$ yields meso-dibromide.
Statement II: cis-But-2-ene $+$ alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ (syn-dihydroxylation) yields meso-butane-2,3-diol.
questions.optionD: Statement I is INCORRECT (Anti addition to trans gives meso, but diagram shows pair) and Statement II is CORRECT
questions.explanation: Syn-dihydroxylation of cis-alkene with Bayer's reagent gives meso product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: 1-Phenylprop-1-yne reduced with $\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$ gives trans-alkene L, while Lindlar's $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd/C}$ gives cis-alkene K. K and L are:
questions.explanation: Birch reduction gives trans-alkene while Lindlar hydrogenation gives stereospecific cis-alkene (diastereomers / geometrical isomers).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which coordination complex exhibits FACIAL ($fac$) and MERIDIONAL ($mer$) geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: Octahedral complexes of the form $[M a_3 b_3]$ (like $[\text{Cr(py)}_3\text{Cl}_3]$) display facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Identify chemical reactions that produce ANILINE as the major product:
B. Benzamide $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}}$ Aniline (Hoffmann degradation)
D. Acetanilide $\xrightarrow{\text{HCl/H}_2\text{O}/\Delta}$ Aniline (Amide hydrolysis)
questions.explanation: Hoffmann bromamide degradation of benzamide and acidic hydrolysis of acetanilide both yield pure aniline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Vitamins with Dietary Sources:
A. Vitamin A, B. Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$, C. Vitamin E, D. Vitamin K
I. Meat / Liver, II. Sunflower oil, III. Green leafy vegetables, IV. Carrots
questions.explanation: Vitamin A = Carrots (IV), $\text{B}_{12}$ = Meat (I), Vitamin E = Sunflower oil (II), Vitamin K = Green leafy vegetables (III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct decreasing order of oxidation state of the underlined atom is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is $+5$, Aluminium in $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is $+3$, and Sulfur in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is $-2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Aldol condensation between 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone and Benzaldehyde CANNOT produce:
questions.explanation: The substituted $\alpha$-position with gem-dimethyl groups has no $\alpha$-hydrogens to form an enolate ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which heptadiene contains CONJUGATED double bonds (alternating double and single bonds)?
questions.explanation: Hepta-1,3-diene has conjugated double bonds separated by a single carbon-carbon bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Oxidation of p-nitrotoluene with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives p-nitrobenzoic acid (stronger than benzoic acid due to $-M/-I$).
Statement II: Reduction of p-nitrotoluene gives p-toluidine (more basic than aniline due to $+I/+H$).
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are TRUE and CORRECT
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing nitro group increases benzoic acidity; electron-donating methyl group enhances toluidine basicity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Thermal decomposition of purple $\text{KMnO}_4$ at $513\text{K}$ produces the green paramagnetic compound:
questions.explanation: $2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{513\text{K}} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\text{ (green)} + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Toluene $\xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{CS}_2, \text{H}_3\text{O}^+} P$ (Benzaldehyde). Compound P can also be prepared by:
questions.optionD: Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride with $\text{H}_2 / \text{Pd-BaSO}_4$
questions.explanation: Etard oxidation yields benzaldehyde, which is also synthesized via Rosenmund catalytic hydrogenolysis of benzoyl chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which coordination complex behaves as a $1 : 3$ electrolyte in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3 \to [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^-$ (produces 1 complex cation and 3 chloride anions).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The radial wavefunction $\psi(r)$ plot exhibiting TWO RADIAL NODES ($n - l - 1 = 2$) is:
questions.optionC: Plot C (Crosses zero twice $\implies$ 2 radial nodes)
questions.explanation: Radial nodes occur where the radial wavefunction $\psi_r$ passes through zero; plot C shows two distinct zero-crossings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Correct increasing order of polarity (dipole moment / dielectric) is:
questions.explanation: Dielectric polarity: Non-polar ether $<$ polar aprotic ketone $<$ hydrogen-bonding alcohol $<$ dimerizing carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) for neon dimer $\text{Ne}_2$ ($20\text{ electrons}$) is:
questions.explanation: Filling all 20 electrons places the last two electrons into the antibonding $\sigma^*_{2p}$ orbital.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The total number of vertebrae in the adult human vertebral column is:
questions.explanation: Adult human vertebral column consists of 26 serially arranged vertebrae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Symbiotic mutualistic associations between fungi and algae are called:
questions.explanation: Lichens represent symbiotic partnerships between a photosynthetic phycobiont (alga/cyanobacterium) and a mycobiont (fungus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The classical Cell Theory was originally formulated by:
questions.explanation: Schleiden (botanist, 1838) and Schwann (zoologist, 1839) jointly formulated the cell doctrine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are cytological features of prokaryotic cells?
(a) 70S ribosomes (50S and 30S subunits)
(b) Extrachromosomal plasmid DNA
(c) Mesosomal membrane invaginations
(d) Peroxisomes (Absent in prokaryotes)
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes contain 70S ribosomes, circular plasmids, and mesosomes; membrane-bound peroxisomes are absent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which anatomical structure is NOT a component of the human central nervous system meninges/brain?
questions.optionD: Pericardium (Protective fibrous sac enclosing the heart)
questions.explanation: Dura mater, arachnoid, and pia mater are cranial meninges; pericardium protects the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The inner mitochondrial membrane encloses the dense homogeneous proteinaceous fluid termed:
questions.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane bounds the central matrix containing Krebs cycle enzymes, 70S ribosomes, and mtDNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Organelles with Morphology:
A. Cristae, B. Cisternae, C. Thylakoids, D. Phospholipid
I. Flattened stroma thylakoid sacs in chloroplast, II. Infoldings of inner mitochondrial membrane, III. Plasma membrane bilayer, IV. Disc-shaped stacked sacs in Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation: Cristae = Mitochondrial folds (II), Cisternae = Golgi cisternae (IV), Thylakoids = Chloroplast sacs (I), Phospholipids = Membrane (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The plastid specialized for storing yellow-orange carotenoid pigments including xanthophylls is:
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts synthesize and accumulate fat-soluble carotenoid and xanthophyll pigments giving yellow/orange color to petals and fruits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding human pituitary gland:
(a) Divided into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) Secretes FSH
(c) Secretes MSH (Melanocyte stimulating hormone)
questions.explanation: Pituitary gland comprises anterior adenohypophysis (secretes FSH, LH, ACTH, PRL, TSH, MSH) and neurohypophysis (releases oxytocin/ADH).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In photorespiration catalyzed by RuBisCO oxygenase: $\text{RuBP} + \text{O}_2 \to 3\text{-PGA} + X$. Substance $X$ is:
questions.explanation: Oxygenation of 5-carbon RuBP yields one molecule of 3-PGA (3C) and one molecule of 2-phosphoglycolate (2C).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (Mad Cow Disease) is caused by infectious proteinaceous particles called:
questions.explanation: Prions are abnormally folded infectious protein particles causing neurodegenerative kuru, Creutzfeldt-Jakob, and mad cow disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The reaction centre chlorophyll a molecule in Photosystem I (PS I) has an absorption peak maximum at:
questions.explanation: The reaction center of PS I consists of a chlorophyll a dimer designated $P_{700}$ with absorbance peak at $700\text{ nm}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: When submerged in water, adult frogs respire exclusively through:
questions.explanation: In aquatic environments, frogs perform gas exchange solely through their highly vascularized moist skin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The anatomical sequence of bones in the human lower hindlimb from proximal to distal is:
questions.explanation: Thigh femur articulates at knee joint with patella and shank tibia/fibula, followed by ankle tarsals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Phyllotaxy refers to the botanical pattern of arrangement of:
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of leaf arrangement (alternate, opposite, or whorled) on the shoot axis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biological Molecules with Functions:
A. Starch, B. Antibody, C. Concanavalin A, D. GLUT-4
I. Fights infection, II. Energy storage polysaccharide, III. Insulin-dependent glucose transport, IV. Plant lectin
questions.explanation: Starch = Storage (II), Antibody = Defense (I), Concanavalin A = Lectin (IV), GLUT-4 = Glucose transport (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Radial symmetry divides body into equal halves through any plane passing through central axis.
Statement II: In echinoderms, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
questions.optionC: Statement I is CORRECT, but Statement II is INCORRECT (Echinoderm larvae are bilaterally symmetrical)
questions.explanation: Echinoderm free-swimming ciliated larvae are bilaterally symmetrical, developing radial symmetry only in adult phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The cellular Endomembrane System in eukaryotes functionally includes:
questions.optionA: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles
questions.explanation: Endomembrane system includes ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles whose functions are coordinated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How many molecules of Pyruvic acid are generated at the end of Glycolysis from 206 molecules of Glucose?
questions.explanation: Each 6-carbon glucose molecule cleaved during glycolysis yields 2 molecules of 3-carbon pyruvic acid: $206 \times 2 = 412$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which synthetic auxin plant growth regulator is widely used as a selective broadleaf herbicide?
questions.explanation: 2,4-D is extensively used as a weedicide to eradicate dicot weeds in cereal monocot crop fields.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: In gymnosperms, male and female gametophytes remain retained within sporangia on sporophyte.
Statement II: Gymnosperm seeds are naked.
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are TRUE and CORRECT
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms lack independent free-living gametophytes (retained on sporophyte) and lack ovaries (seeds are naked).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Bacterial Morphological Shapes:
A. Spherical, B. Rod-shaped, C. Comma-shaped, D. Spiral
I. Vibrio, II. Cocci, III. Spirilla, IV. Bacilli
questions.explanation: Spherical = Cocci (II), Rod = Bacilli (IV), Comma = Vibrio (I), Spiral = Spirilla (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Characteristic floral features of family Solanaceae include:
(a) Bisexual, actinomorphic flowers
(b) Gamosepalous calyx with 5 persistent sepals
(c) 5 epipetalous stamens
(d) Superior bicarpellary ovary (Inferior is incorrect)
questions.explanation: Solanaceae flowers are bisexual, actinomorphic, with 5 united sepals, 5 epipetalous stamens, and superior ovary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Historical chronological sequence of photosynthesis discoveries is:
questions.optionB: Role of air (Priestley) $\to$ Release of oxygen (Ingenhousz) $\to$ Glucose synthesis (Sachs) $\to$ Action spectra (Engelmann)
questions.explanation: Joseph Priestley (1770) $\to$ Jan Ingenhousz (1779) $\to$ Julius von Sachs (1854) $\to$ T.W. Engelmann (1888).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Normal intrinsic firing rate of action potentials generated by Sino-Atrial Node (SAN) in human heart is:
questions.explanation: The SA node pacemaker initiates regular rhythmic myogenic cardiac action potentials at $70-75\text{ beats/min}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How many turns of the Calvin cycle ($C_3$ path) are required to synthesize THREE molecules of Glucose?
questions.explanation: One glucose molecule requires 6 turns of Calvin cycle ($6\text{ CO}_2$ fixed); three glucose molecules require $3 \times 6 = 18$ turns.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding blood coagulation cascade is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: Blood coagulates in response to trauma
questions.optionC: Fibrin is produced from inactive fibrinogen by thrombin
questions.optionD: Fibrinogen is produced from fibrin (Fibrin is formed from fibrinogen)
questions.explanation: Thrombin enzyme cleaves soluble plasma fibrinogen into insoluble polymerized fibrin threads forming the clot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Mango (Mangifera indica) Taxonomic Hierarchy:
A. Family, B. Genus, C. Class, D. Phylum/Division, E. Order
I. Sapindales, II. Dicotyledonae, III. Anacardiaceae, IV. Angiospermae, V. Mangifera
questions.explanation: Family = Anacardiaceae (III), Genus = Mangifera (V), Class = Dicotyledonae (II), Division = Angiospermae (IV), Order = Sapindales (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Arrange taxonomic categories in ascending hierarchical order:
questions.optionA: Species (g) $\to$ Genus (a) $\to$ Family (e) $\to$ Order (c) $\to$ Class (b) $\to$ Phylum (d) $\to$ Kingdom (f)
questions.explanation: Ascending Linnaean hierarchy: Species $\to$ Genus $\to$ Family $\to$ Order $\to$ Class $\to$ Phylum/Division $\to$ Kingdom.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Placentation Types with Botanical Examples:
A. Marginal, B. Axile, C. Parietal, D. Free central
I. Argemone, II. Tomato, III. Primrose / Dianthus, IV. Pea
questions.explanation: Marginal = Pea (IV), Axile = Tomato (II), Parietal = Argemone (I), Free central = Primrose (III).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Sphenopsida (Horsetails, Equisetum) belongs to which botanical division?
questions.explanation: Pteridophyta is divided into Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida (Equisetum), and Pteropsida.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which statements regarding C2 Photorespiration are correct?
(c) 2-Phosphoglycolate is synthesized
(d) No ATP or NADPH is generated (Wasteful dissipative pathway)
questions.explanation: Photorespiration occurs in C3 plants under high $O_2$, fixing oxygen to produce phosphoglycolate without ATP/NADPH yield.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is the major subcellular site for:
questions.optionB: Synthesis of lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones
questions.explanation: SER synthesizes neutral lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones (like androgens/estrogens).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT endocrine physiological statement:
questions.optionA: $\alpha$-cells of islets of Langerhans secrete glucagon
questions.optionB: $\alpha$-cells of pancreas secrete insulin ($\beta$-cells secrete insulin)
questions.explanation: Pancreatic beta cells secrete insulin; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In biological taxonomy, a Genus represents:
questions.optionC: A group of closely related species sharing correlated characters
questions.explanation: Genus comprises an assemblage of closely related species having more characters in common than species of other genera.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following organisms is a EUKARYOTE (not a prokaryote)?
questions.optionD: Fungi (Eukaryotic heterotrophs with chitinous cell walls)
questions.explanation: Fungi are true eukaryotic organisms with membrane-bound nuclei and organellar compartments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which plant growth regulator promotes rapid internode elongation ('bolting') prior to flowering in rosette plants like cabbage?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins stimulate rapid cell elongation and bolting in rosette plants (cabbage, beet) before flowering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The correct sequence of phases in the eukaryotic adult cell cycle is:
questions.optionC: G1 phase $\to$ S phase $\to$ G2 phase $\to$ M phase (Mitosis)
questions.explanation: Interphase starts with $G_1$ (growth), proceeds through $S$ (replication) and $G_2$ (mitotic preparation), culminating in $M$ phase division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Fungal Sexual Stages with Terminology:
A. Protoplasmic fusion of two gametes, B. Fusion of two haploid nuclei, C. Meiotic formation of haploid spores
I. Meiosis, II. Plasmogamy, III. Karyogamy
questions.explanation: Plasmogamy = Cytoplasm fusion (II), Karyogamy = Nuclear fusion (III), Meiosis = Spore reduction division (I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: The class name Reptilia refers to creeping/crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II: All reptiles have a 3-chambered heart.
questions.optionC: Statement I is CORRECT but Statement II is INCORRECT (Crocodiles have a 4-chambered heart)
questions.explanation: Reptilia refers to creeping locomotion (Latin repere); crocodiles possess a four-chambered heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Chromosomes reach terminal condensation at the end of diakinesis (prophase I).
Statement II: Meiosis I resembles equational mitosis.
questions.optionC: Statement I is TRUE, but Statement II is FALSE (Meiosis I is reductional; Meiosis II resembles mitosis)
questions.explanation: Diakinesis marks full chromosome condensation. Meiosis I is reductional segregation of homologues; Meiosis II is equational like mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental chordate characteristic?
questions.optionC: Absence of pharyngeal gill slits (Presence of paired pharyngeal slits is a chordate hallmark)
questions.explanation: All chordates possess notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits, and post-anal tail at some developmental stage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Plant shoot initial length is $20\text{ cm}$. With arithmetic growth rate $30\text{ cm/day}$, length at end of 7 days ($L_t = L_0 + rt$) is:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Arrange elemental abundance in human body in descending order of weight percentage:
questions.explanation: Human body elemental weight: Oxygen ($65\%$) $>$ Carbon ($18.5\%$) $>$ Nitrogen/Hydrogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The number of pairs of Cranial Nerves originating from the brain in frogs is:
questions.explanation: Frogs (amphibians) have 10 pairs of cranial nerves; amniotes (reptiles, birds, mammals) have 12 pairs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which microbial therapeutic enzyme is clinically administered as a 'clot buster'?
questions.explanation: Streptokinase dissolves blood clots (thrombi) in patients suffering from myocardial infarction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Inactive Bt crystalline protoxin is solubilized and activated in insect digestive system:
questions.optionA: Due to alkaline pH of insect midgut
questions.explanation: Alkaline pH of the insect midgut solubilizes Bt protoxin crystals into active toxic fragments that perforate gut epithelium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Down's syndrome is caused by absence of X chromosome.
Statement II: Turner's syndrome is caused by an additional chromosome.
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are INCORRECT / FALSE
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is trisomy 21 (extra autosome); Turner's syndrome is monosomy X ($45, XO$ absence of sex chromosome).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which infectious disease is NOT sexually transmitted?
questions.optionB: Tuberculosis (Airborne respiratory droplet infection by Mycobacterium)
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is transmitted via respiratory aerosol droplets, whereas syphilis, gonorrhoea, and genital warts are STIs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Propulsive motility of mammalian spermatozoa through the female reproductive tract is driven by:
questions.optionA: Flagellar movement (Axoneme microtubule sliding in sperm tail)
questions.explanation: The sperm tail flagellum beats with whip-like undulating waves to propel sperm forward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Natural selection in a population can operate through which evolutionary modes?
(a) Stabilising selection
(c) Directional selection
(d) Disruptive selection
questions.optionB: (a), (c) and (d) only (Stabilising, Directional, and Disruptive selection)
questions.explanation: Natural selection produces stabilizing (narrowing mean), directional (shift toward one extreme), or disruptive (favoring both extremes) outcomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) procedure where a single sperm is injected directly into ovum cytoplasm is:
questions.explanation: ICSI is a micromanipulation IVF technique where an isolated sperm is directly microinjected into an unfertilized egg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which anatomical structure is part of the FEMALE reproductive tract (not male)?
questions.optionD: Infundibulum (Funnel-shaped part of Fallopian tube / Oviduct)
questions.explanation: Infundibulum with fimbriae is the ovarian end of female fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Arrange Amazonian rainforest biodiversity in descending order of species richness:
questions.explanation: Amazon species count: Invertebrates ($>125,000$) $>$ Plants ($40,000$) $>$ Fishes ($3,000$) $>$ Birds ($1,300$) $>$ Mammals ($427$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Ovulation is triggered by mid-cycle LH surge causing Graafian follicle rupture.
Statement II: Remnant luteal tissue secretes large amounts of estrogen.
questions.optionC: Statement I is TRUE, but Statement II is FALSE (Corpus luteum primarily secretes large amounts of Progesterone)
questions.explanation: LH surge triggers ovulation; the resulting corpus luteum secretes primarily progesterone for endometrial maintenance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In a grazing food chain, PRIMARY CONSUMERS feeding directly on autotrophic producers are:
questions.explanation: Herbivores eat primary producers (plants) and occupy the second trophic level ($T_2$) as primary consumers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, if allele frequency of dominant allele $A$ is $p = 0.1$, the frequency of homozygous genotype $AA$ ($p^2$) is:
questions.explanation: Frequency of homozygous dominant $AA = p^2 = (0.1)^2 = 0.01$ ($1\%$ of population).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Endocrine Hormones with Clinical/Physiological Actions:
A. Excess GH, B. LH, C. Vasopressin (ADH), D. Oxytocin
I. Renal water/electrolyte reabsorption, II. Uterine myometrial contraction during parturition, III. Acromegaly in adults, IV. Ovulation & corpus luteum maintenance
questions.explanation: Excess GH = Acromegaly (III), LH = Ovulation (IV), Vasopressin = Water reabsorption (I), Oxytocin = Uterine contraction (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The atrioventricular orifice between right atrium and right ventricle of human heart is guarded by:
questions.explanation: Tricuspid valve guards right atrioventricular opening; bicuspid (mitral) valve guards left opening.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Primitive aquatic Sponges (Phylum Porifera) perform respiration and gas exchange via:
questions.optionA: Simple diffusion over their entire moist body surfaces
questions.explanation: Sponges lack specialized respiratory organs; water circulating through spongeocoel allows direct cellular diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A typical bilobed angiosperm anther is dithecous, meaning EACH anther lobe possesses:
questions.optionA: 2 thecae (Dithecous, with 2 microsporangia per lobe $\implies$ tetrasporangiate anther)
questions.explanation: Each lobe of a dithecous anther contains two thecae separated by a longitudinal groove.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling is initiated at neuromuscular junctions by neural release of:
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine released into the synaptic cleft binds nicotinic ACh receptors on the sarcolemma, generating an action potential.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding regulation of the lac operon is TRUE?
questions.optionA: The regulatory i gene is constitutively transcribed and expressed all the time
questions.explanation: The lacI gene has its own promoter and is expressed constitutively to maintain basal levels of lac repressor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which cellular structures in the angiosperm female gametophyte guide the pollen tube toward the egg?
questions.explanation: Filiform apparatus of synergids secretes chemotropic attractants that guide pollen tube entry into embryo sac.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following plants produces NON-ALBUMINOUS (exalbuminous) seeds lacking persistent endosperm?
questions.explanation: Pea, gram, and bean seeds completely consume endosperm during embryo development, storing reserves in cotyledons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If the diploid somatic chromosome number of an angiosperm is $2n = 36$, chromosome number in triploid endosperm is:
questions.explanation: Haploid number $n = 36/2 = 18$. Triploid endosperm ($3n$) contains $3 \times 18 = 54$ chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct physiological statements on Henle's loop reabsorption:
(a) Descending limb permeable to water, impermeable to salts
(b) Medullary countercurrent multiplier concentrates tubular fluid
(d) Ascending limb conducts active/passive electrolyte reabsorption
questions.explanation: Descending limb reabsorbs water; ascending limb reabsorbs NaCl (impermeable to water), concentrating urine in the medulla.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Correct anatomical sequence of human vertebral column from cranial to caudal is:
questions.explanation: Vertebral column order from head to toe: 7 Cervical $\to$ 12 Thoracic $\to$ 5 Lumbar $\to$ 1 Sacrum $\to$ 1 Coccyx.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following was rejected as scientific evidence for evolution?
questions.optionC: Biogenetic Law / Embryological recapitulation proposed by Ernst Haeckel (Disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer)
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel's 'ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny' was rejected after von Baer demonstrated embryos never pass through adult stages of other animals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Modern Homo sapiens arose in Australia and migrated.
Statement II: Modern Homo sapiens arose around 75,000 to 10,000 years ago during the ice age.
questions.optionD: Statement I is INCORRECT (Arose in Africa) but Statement II is CORRECT
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens evolved in Africa and spread across continents during the ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In a cell population of 10 million with equal birth rate ($0.002$) and death rate ($0.002$), population after 10 generations is:
questions.optionC: 10 million (Zero intrinsic rate of growth $r = b - d = 0$)
questions.explanation: Since birth rate equals death rate ($b = d$), net intrinsic growth rate $r = 0$, maintaining constant population size.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), sequence-specific synthetic oligonucleotide primers bind to single-stranded template DNA during:
questions.explanation: During annealing step at $50-60^\circ\text{C}$, forward and reverse primers hybridize to complementary $3'$ ends of single-stranded DNA templates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: Logistic population growth model is more realistic than exponential growth.
Reason R: Environmental resources (food, space) in natural habitats are finite and limiting.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: No population can grow exponentially indefinitely because natural resources are limited, imposing a carrying capacity $K$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Adaptive radiation of Australian marsupials paralleling placental mammals occupying similar ecological niches exemplifies:
questions.explanation: Independent adaptive radiations in geographically isolated marsupials and placentals produced convergent analogous ecotypes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following are SECONDARY lymphoid organs where mature lymphocytes encounter antigens?
questions.optionD: Bone marrow and thymus (Primary lymphoid organs)
questions.explanation: Bone marrow and thymus are primary generative lymphoid organs; spleen, tonsils, lymph nodes, and Peyer's patches are secondary lymphoid tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following hormones is NOT synthesized or secreted by the human placenta?
questions.optionD: Luteinizing Hormone (LH, secreted by anterior pituitary)
questions.explanation: Placenta secretes hCG, hPL, estrogens, progesterone, and relaxin; LH is secreted by anterior pituitary gonadotrophs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which RNA Polymerase enzyme transcribes eukaryotic precursor heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA / pre-mRNA)?
questions.explanation: RNA Polymerase II transcribes all protein-coding pre-mRNAs and hnRNAs in eukaryotic nuclei.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Plasmids are autonomously replicating circular DNA.
Statement II: Plasmids are extrachromosomal genetic elements in bacteria.
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are TRUE and CORRECT
questions.explanation: Bacterial plasmids are extrachromosomal double-stranded circular DNA molecules that replicate autonomously.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A child with blood group 'O' ($ii$) CANNOT be born to which parental genotype combination?
questions.optionD: Father $I^A I^B$ and Mother $I^A i$ (Father AB lacks recessive $i$ allele)
questions.explanation: Parent with $I^A I^B$ (blood group AB) can only pass $I^A$ or $I^B$, making it impossible to conceive a child with genotype $ii$ (blood group O).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: Forelimbs of humans and bats are homologous organs.
Reason R: Forelimbs of humans and bats share similar fundamental pentadactyl anatomical bone architecture.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: Human arms and bat wings share humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, and digits, reflecting divergent evolution from a common mammalian ancestor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Colostrum yellowish fluid secreted by mammary glands during first days of lactation is rich in protective antibody:
questions.optionC: Secretory IgA (Provides passive mucosal immunity to infant)
questions.explanation: Colostrum provides high concentrations of secretory IgA antibodies conferring passive immunity to the newborn's GI tract.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: Abingdon tortoises in Galapagos became extinct within a decade after goats were introduced.
Reason R: Goats had superior browsing efficiency, depleting finite vegetation.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: Interspecific resource competition by introduced goats drove endemic tortoises to extinction on Galapagos islands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The non-cellular glycoprotein coat surrounding secondary oocyte at ovulation is:
questions.explanation: Ovulated secondary oocyte is encased by inner zona pellucida and outer cellular corona radiata.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Interspecific Interactions:
A. Both species harmed, B. One harmed and other benefited, C. Both benefited, D. One benefited other unaffected
I. Predation/Parasitism, II. Mutualism, III. Competition, IV. Commensalism
questions.explanation: Competition = $-/-$ (III), Predation = $+/-$ (I), Mutualism = $+/+$ (II), Commensalism = $+/0$ (IV).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: In Mendel's monohybrid cross, all $F_1$ progeny are tall and none are dwarf.
Reason R: Tall allele ($T$) is completely dominant over recessive dwarf allele ($t$).
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: Law of Dominance: in a heterozygous state ($Tt$), the dominant tall allele masks expression of recessive dwarf allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion A: In rDNA technology, lysozyme lyses bacterial cell walls while cellulase digests plant walls.
Reason R: Isolation of pure high-molecular weight genomic DNA requires enzymatic cell wall breakdown.
questions.optionA: Both A and R are CORRECT and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
questions.explanation: Lysozyme hydrolyzes bacterial peptidoglycan and cellulase digests plant cellulose to release cellular DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which opioid derivative is clinically utilized as a potent post-surgical analgesic and sedative?
questions.explanation: Morphine is a central opioid agonist prescribed for managing acute severe post-operative pain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Select correct statements regarding Ecological Energy Flow:
(a) Energy flow through trophic levels is strictly unidirectional
(b) Pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted
questions.explanation: Energy flow follows Lindeman's 10% law (not 1%); energy pyramids are strictly upright with unidirectional flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding life cycle of Plasmodium malaria parasite is TRUE?
questions.optionD: Fertilization and zygote (ookinete) formation take place in mosquito gut lumen
questions.explanation: Sexual fertilization occurs in female Anopheles mosquito gut, producing motile ookinete and oocyst.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Recombinant Cloning Components:
A. Transformation, B. Cloning site, C. Selection, D. Ori
I. Restriction endonuclease recognition sequence, II. Introducing recombinant DNA into bacterial host, III. Origin of replication initiation, IV. Selectable antibiotic marker
questions.explanation: Transformation = DNA uptake (II), Cloning site = Restriction site (I), Selection = Antibiotic resistance (IV), Ori = Replication origin (III).
